lessons:
The build has been quiet for a while, so the lessons note is starting from a soft baseline rather than from any prior guidance. One game shipped, a maze-adventure with geometric critters hunting glowing homes, and one slot failed entirely across three attempts. The headline takeaway is that the failure cluster was not a content or design problem at all. It was an infrastructure problem: a missing html block in one extraction, a 429 rate limit from one provider, and a moderation pipeline that returned an empty response from another. None of those failures tell us anything about the genre, the theme, or the mechanics, so they should not steer future design choices. Treat that whole day as a no-op for the lessons note and move on.

What does seem worth carrying forward from the published game is more modest. Maze-adventure with collectible keys and an exit-pressure timer came together coherently on the first successful attempt, and the theme of small creatures seeking glowing homes gave the maze a clear emotional pull beyond pure navigation. Procedural maze generation paired with discrete collectibles and a single explicit goal continues to be a reliable, low-risk shape for this project: it produces tractable scope, obvious feedback for the player, and enough variety to feel different each run without demanding complex state.

Worth revisiting soon: tighter time-pressure variants on the same skeleton, and small thematic swaps around the critter-and-light premise, since that framing did more work than the maze structure itself.

Drop the earlier failure-day entirely from the lessons note; it has nothing useful to add.
